definitions.window: For n>=2 and k>=1, window W(n,k) = {n, ..., n+k-1}.
definitions.property: n is an exceptional start for k iff every member of W(n,k) has all prime factors <= k, and (n==2 or W(n-1,k) does not have that property).

claim: A clean run of the verifier (verify(WITNESS) returning without raising) establishes the finite-computational fragment of L1: exact integer arithmetic certifies that for k=2,3,4 on [2,10^6] the only windows with no member having a prime factor >k start exactly at n=2,8 (k=2), n=8,24 (k=3), n=24 (k=4), extremality included. covers=fragment: the analytic k=2 all-n>=2 argument (no consecutive powers of 2) and any transfer to the canonical clause-2 limsup are NOT certified here.
law: Wang 7.2: an exact finite object plus a proved reduction is a CERTIFICATE. The reduction is the `claim` and is a human's to audit; the object and the verifier run are the machine's part.
